overview: Jacobs Solutions is a global professional services firm providing consulting, engineering, architecture, program/construction management and advisory services to public- and private-sector clients across infrastructure, advanced facilities (data centers, semiconductors, life sciences), water, energy, transportation and government/defense markets. Founded in 1947 and headquartered in Dallas, Texas, the company operates through two reporting segments -- Infrastructure & Advanced Facilities (I&AF) and PA Consulting (fully owned since March 2026) -- with roughly $12 billion of FY2025 revenue and a record backlog above $28.9 billion as of Q3 FY2026 (fiscal year ends late September). Jacobs completed a major portfolio transformation in 2024-2025, divesting its Critical Mission Solutions (government IT/cyber) and Cyber & Intelligence businesses to focus on higher-margin infrastructure, advanced facilities and consulting work, and has since become a prominent beneficiary of AI/data-center capital spending.

business_model.summary: Jacobs earns fee-based revenue from professional services contracts (engineering design, program/construction management, consulting and advisory) rather than from taking construction or balance-sheet risk on projects, giving it an asset-light, people-driven model with a large multi-year backlog that provides revenue visibility. Following the 2024 divestiture of its lower-margin government-services (Critical Mission Solutions/Cyber & Intelligence) business and the March 2026 buy-in of the remaining PA Consulting stake, the mix has shifted toward higher-margin, less commoditized advisory and technical-consulting work. Reported gross revenue includes significant pass-through subcontractor/procurement costs; management's preferred metric, "adjusted net revenue," strips these out and is the basis for guidance and margin targets.

revenue_streams.name: Infrastructure & Advanced Facilities (data centers, semiconductors, life sciences/advanced manufacturing, water, transportation, energy & power)
revenue_streams.trend: growing, accelerating (Q3 FY26 net revenue +10% organic YoY, record quarter)

revenue_streams.name: PA Consulting (management/technology/innovation consulting)
revenue_streams.trend: growing; fully consolidated since March 2026 buy-in of remaining ~35% stake

revenue_streams.name: Direct AI/data-center infrastructure work (cuts across I&AF)
revenue_streams.trend: rapidly growing -- up ~100bps sequentially in Q3 FY26; pipeline reported up ~400% YoY

business_model.customer_type: Mixed public and private sector: hyperscalers and private data-center/semiconductor developers, life sciences and advanced-manufacturing corporates, water utilities and municipalities, U.S. and allied governments (transportation, defense-adjacent infrastructure, environmental), and large corporates buying PA Consulting advisory services. Contracts are typically long-cycle, project- and program-based rather than subscription revenue, but the large multi-year backlog (~$28.9B, 1.4x TTM book-to-bill) functions similarly to a revenue-visibility backlog in a recurring-demand industry.
business_model.geographic_mix: Predominantly North America and the UK/Europe, with operations extending to the Middle East, Asia-Pacific, Australia/New Zealand and India; PA Consulting adds UK/European advisory exposure.

main_competitors: Accenture / Deloitte / consulting firms (for PA Consulting overlap)
competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest global engineering/professional-services firms by revenue, with a leading position in data-center and advanced-facilities design/delivery, water infrastructure, and U.S. federal/state transportation work; no single competitor dominates the fragmented global engineering-services market, and Jacobs frequently partners with the same firms it competes against on large joint ventures.

moat_factors.description: Ability to staff and deliver very large, complex, multi-discipline programs (hyperscale data centers, semiconductor fabs, water systems) that few competitors can match end-to-end.

Record $28.9B backlog (1.4x TTM book-to-bill) with multi-year visibility into 2027-2028 on AI/data-center work provides revenue durability and repeat business with hyperscalers and government agencies.

moat_factors.factor: Reputation, safety record and technical accreditation
moat_factors.description: Engineering and program-management work for critical infrastructure (nuclear, water, defense-adjacent, semiconductor cleanrooms) requires accumulated track record and security clearances that are slow for new entrants to replicate.
Once engaged as designer/program manager on a multi-year capital program, incumbency and institutional knowledge make it costly for clients to switch mid-stream.

Full ownership of PA Consulting (closed March 2026, ~13x EBITDA) is intended to bundle higher-margin digital/strategy advisory with core engineering delivery, a differentiator versus pure-play engineering peers.

weaknesses: People-intensive, asset-light model means limited pricing power on commoditized engineering scopes and margin sensitive to talent costs/utilization
Meaningful exposure to U.S. federal/state government infrastructure and environmental spending, which is subject to budget cycles, continuing resolutions, and policy shifts

Data-center/AI capex is a large and increasingly important growth driver (11% of adjusted net revenue and rising) but concentrates cyclicality risk in a narrow, fast-growing, and potentially frothy end market

Complex post-divestiture/post-acquisition reporting (Critical Mission Solutions divested 2024, PA Consulting minority buy-in 2026) complicates historical trend comparability and elevated the effective tax rate temporarily in FY2026
Lower brand/scale versus the largest global EPC/construction players (Bechtel, Fluor) on fixed-price, construction-risk-bearing mega-projects, a segment Jacobs largely avoids by design

growth_drivers: AI/data-center capital spending supercycle: direct AI-infrastructure work is 11% of adjusted net revenue and rising ~100bps/quarter; management cites a data-center pipeline up 2-3x and AI-infrastructure pipeline up ~400% YoY, with visibility into 2027-2028
Life sciences and advanced manufacturing: strongest-ever segment growth (+24% in Q3 FY2026) as pharma/biotech and semiconductor fabrication capacity expands in the US
Water infrastructure: aging water/wastewater systems in the US and UK, PFAS remediation, and utility capital programs provide a long, largely non-discretionary growth runway

PA Consulting full ownership: expected to be EPS-accretive within 12 months of the March 2026 close, lift adjusted margins ~60bps, and generate $20M+ of cost synergies (raised from an original $16-20M estimate) within 24 months
Semiconductor/advanced manufacturing reshoring driven by US CHIPS-era incentives and private capex
Continued capital return: $614M of buybacks year-to-date through Q3 FY2026 alongside deleveraging
Margin expansion from portfolio mix shift toward higher-margin advisory/consulting and away from lower-margin government IT services divested in 2024

business.description: A rapidly growing share of revenue (11% and climbing) is tied to hyperscaler and private data-center capital spending; any slowdown, pause, or AI-capex retrenchment (a live macro debate in 2026) would disproportionately hit the fastest-growing part of the business.

Transportation, water and other public infrastructure work depends on federal/state/municipal appropriations, which are subject to political and fiscal-year budget risk, including US government funding uncertainty.

People-based model is exposed to engineering-labor shortages and wage inflation, particularly given the surge in demand from AI-infrastructure and semiconductor projects competing for the same skilled workforce.

Fragmented market with well-capitalized competitors (AECOM, WSP, Stantec, Fluor, Bechtel) bidding for the same large programs; Jacobs must compete on price, technical capability, and delivery track record.

financial.risk: Elevated effective tax rate post-PA Consulting
financial.description: GAAP net earnings in Q3 FY2026 declined YoY ($137.4M vs $181.2M) due to a temporarily higher tax rate tied to the PA Consulting acquisition structure, even as adjusted earnings rose -- a reconciling item investors must track.

The ~$1.6B cash-and-stock PA Consulting acquisition (closed March 2026) added debt; management states deleveraging is underway alongside continued buybacks, but net debt/EBITDA (~2.7x per screen data) bears watching.
UK/European operations (especially PA Consulting) and international infrastructure work create GBP/EUR translation exposure against USD-reported results.

regulatory.description: Public-sector infrastructure and defense-adjacent work is subject to procurement regulation, protest risk, and potential policy shifts (e.g., changes to infrastructure or climate-related spending priorities) that can delay or reduce awards.
Legacy environmental remediation and engineering work carries professional-liability and environmental-regulation exposure typical of the industry.

macro.description: Much of Jacobs' end-demand (data centers, manufacturing, private infrastructure) depends on clients' cost of capital and capex appetite; sustained high rates could slow project sanctioning even as backlog remains strong.

macro.risk: AI capex cycle turn / hyperscaler spending discipline
macro.description: A broader market concern in 2026 is whether hyperscaler AI capital spending is sustainable; Jacobs' AI/data-center revenue share has been a key re-rating driver, making the stock sensitive to sentiment shifts on AI infrastructure spending durability.

While backlog and long-cycle contracts provide some buffer, a broad recession would eventually pressure private capex-driven segments (data centers, advanced manufacturing) and could delay public infrastructure funding.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global engineering/infrastructure-services demand remains robust, driven by AI/data-center buildout, semiconductor reshoring, water-infrastructure renewal, energy transition/grid investment, and public infrastructure programs (US IIJA-era funding still flowing). Jacobs' record $28.9B backlog and 1.4x trailing book-to-bill (as of Q3 FY2026) reflect a favorable multi-year demand environment, with management citing visibility into 2027-2028 for AI-infrastructure work specifically.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate. Public infrastructure and water spending are relatively non-cyclical/policy-driven, providing ballast, while data-center, semiconductor and advanced-manufacturing capex are more sensitive to corporate capital-spending cycles and financing conditions -- and are becoming a larger share of the mix.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity via clients' cost of capital and project sanctioning decisions (particularly private data-center/manufacturing capex); direct balance-sheet sensitivity is manageable given moderate leverage and continued deleveraging alongside the PA Consulting acquisition financing.
key_input_costs: Skilled engineering/technical labor and wage inflation
Subcontractor/procurement costs (pass-through, embedded in gross revenue but not adjusted net revenue)
Technology/digital tooling investment (AI-enabled design, digital twins)

recent_developments.event: Reported record Q3 results: gross revenue +34.5% YoY to ~$4.1B, adjusted net revenue +8.3% YoY (~8%+ organic) to $2.4B, adjusted EPS $1.84 (+13.6% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA margin exceeded 15%, up 100+bps YoY. Record backlog of $28.9B (+27% YoY), TTM book-to-bill 1.4x. Free cash flow $541M for the quarter; $142M of Q3 buybacks ($614M YTD). Life sciences/advanced manufacturing grew a record 24%; direct AI/data-center work reached 11% of adjusted net revenue.

Raised FY2026 guidance for the third consecutive quarter: adjusted net revenue growth to 9.5%-10.0% (from 8.0%-10.5%), adjusted EBITDA margin to 14.7%-14.8%, adjusted EPS to $7.20-$7.30 (implying ~19% YoY EPS growth at the midpoint), adjusted FCF margin to ~8%.
Reported ~22% adjusted EPS growth and a then-record ~$27B backlog, driven by the AI-infrastructure boom; raised full-year guidance for the second consecutive quarter.

Completed the ~$1.6B (£1.216B) acquisition of the remaining ~35% stake in PA Consulting (having held 65% since 2021), valuing 100% of PA Consulting at ~£3.05B (13.0x CY2025 EBITDA pre-synergies, 12.3x including synergies); paid 80% cash / 20% stock plus deferred consideration in Jacobs shares. Deal expected to be EPS-accretive within 12 months and lift adjusted margins ~60bps; cost-synergy estimate since raised to $20M+ within 24 months.

Management repeatedly flagged the AI/data-center capex cycle as still early-stage, with data-center pipeline reported up 2-3x and the AI-infrastructure-specific pipeline up ~400% YoY, with revenue visibility extending into 2027-2028.

Completed the strategic divestiture of the Critical Mission Solutions (government IT/cyber) business, part of a multi-year portfolio shift toward higher-margin infrastructure, advanced facilities, and consulting; this reshaped the revenue base (note: FY2024/FY2025 CSV figures show discontinued-operations effects and a swing to a net loss in a transition quarter).

items.vs_prior: raised from 8.0%-10.5% (narrowed and raised midpoint) -- third consecutive quarterly raise
items.notes: Organic growth driven by Infrastructure & Advanced Facilities (data centers, semiconductors, life sciences, water) plus consolidated PA Consulting.
Reflects mix shift toward higher-margin advisory (PA Consulting) and operating leverage in I&AF.
Implies ~19% YoY growth at the midpoint. YTD (9 months) adjusted EPS was $5.12.
Q3 FCF alone was $541M; supports continued buybacks and deleveraging.

items.target: ~11% of adjusted net revenue, trending higher
items.notes: Management does not guide this explicitly as a target but flags it each quarter as a key growth indicator; pipeline visibility cited into 2027-2028.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Bob Pragada characterized the AI/data-center investment cycle as still in its early stages, citing a data-center pipeline up 2-3x and an AI-infrastructure pipeline up roughly 400% YoY with visibility well into 2027-2028. Management highlighted diversified growth across data centers, semiconductors, energy & power, water, and life sciences/advanced manufacturing (a record 24% growth quarter), alongside continued capital return (~$614M of YTD buybacks) and progress integrating PA Consulting, where the cost-synergy estimate was raised to $20M+ within 24 months.

bull_case: Direct beneficiary of the AI/data-center capital-spending supercycle, with a fast-growing, high-visibility revenue stream (11% of adjusted net revenue and rising) backed by a pipeline management says is up several-fold YoY with visibility into 2027-2028
Record backlog of $28.9B and a 1.4x trailing book-to-bill ratio provide unusually strong multi-year revenue visibility for a professional-services business, reducing near-term earnings risk

Three consecutive quarters of raised FY2026 guidance (revenue growth, margin, and EPS all moving higher) demonstrate positive, broad-based momentum across data centers, semiconductors, life sciences/advanced manufacturing, and water

Portfolio transformation (divesting lower-margin government IT/Critical Mission Solutions in 2024, buying full ownership of higher-margin PA Consulting in 2026) is structurally improving margins and revenue quality, with PA Consulting expected to be accretive within 12 months of closing

Diversified end-market exposure (water, life sciences, transportation, energy, advanced manufacturing) beyond AI/data centers reduces single-theme dependency versus some pure-play data-center infrastructure peers, while active buybacks ($614M YTD) return capital to shareholders
bear_case: Growing reliance on AI/data-center capex concentrates risk in a narrow, fast-growing end market; any pause, digestion period, or reassessment of hyperscaler AI spending sustainability (an active 2026 market debate) would disproportionately hit Jacobs' fastest-growing, most highly-valued growth driver

Stock already trades near/above consensus analyst price targets in places (average target ~$164-165 vs. ~$143 share price in September 2026, but with dispersion), implying much of the AI-infrastructure growth story may already be reflected in valuation, and any guidance disappointment could trigger a sharp re-rating

People-intensive, asset-light model has structurally modest margins (~15% adjusted EBITDA margin) versus higher-margin software/consulting-pure-play peers, and is exposed to engineering-labor cost inflation amid surging industry-wide demand for the same skilled talent pool

Government/public-sector infrastructure and water spending, a meaningful and more defensive part of the mix, remains subject to budget and policy risk that could offset some of the AI-driven upside if fiscal conditions tighten

Post-PA Consulting integration and leverage: GAAP earnings were temporarily depressed by a higher tax rate tied to the acquisition structure, and continued M&A/debt-funded growth (after a ~$1.6B, 13x-EBITDA PA Consulting buy-in) adds execution and balance-sheet risk even as management says deleveraging is underway
